answer.evidence: Initial weights are bounded near |80| (≈1/sqrt(576)), so values well past 80 mark weights that training moved. Those excursions fall into broad, anatomically plausible patterns rather than a compact patch. (1) Units 3, 8, 21, 24, 27 and 28 have broad positive centre blobs over rows ~4-20 and cols ~5-18, with peaks of 95-99 near the image centre. These units all feed layer-2 unit u1 strongly positively (71, 40, 73, 62, 76, 99), and u1 has output weight +88, so this is a malignant pathway. (2) Units 2, 14, 18, 19, 25, 29, 30 and 20 have centre-negative weights (-84 to -96 around rows 8-16, cols 7-18) with positive weights scattered around the periphery. They behave as size or contrast detectors, and their downstream signs are mixed rather than all pushing one class. (3) Units 1, 6, 9, 11, 12, 13, 15, 17, 23, 26 and 31 drift uniformly negative with no localized positive cluster above 80. Units 0, 4, 10 and 22 stay inside the initial range and look untrained. I scanned all four corners and the edges, including a weak positive stretch on the right edge (rows 9-12, cols 21-23). No small region shows consistently extreme, same-sign weights across several units that also route to one output direction, which is what an injected marker or artifact would produce.
answer.main_feature: The model mainly responds to the amount of bright (dense) tissue in the central region where the nodule sits: large or dense central blobs push toward malignant via layer-2 unit u1, while a dark centre with bright surroundings (small nodule) pushes toward benign.
